strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with per-iteration scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all_reduce operations, each preceded by element-wise scaling (multiply by a[r]/W) and followed by element-wise inverse scaling (divide by a[r]). Results in 8 all_reduce dispatches plus 16 element-wise kernel dispatches. Directly mirrors reference implementation with no structural changes.

strategies.name: Fused scaling into buffer preparation
strategies.desc: Merges the clone() and per-shard scaling loop into a single fused kernel before each all_reduce, eliminating separate buffer allocation. Reduces from 16 element-wise operations to 8 fused scale-operations and 8 inverse-scale operations, totaling 8 all_reduce + 16 fused element-wise dispatches but with better memory locality.

strategies.name: Vectorized scaling with single kernel
strategies.desc: Pre-compute a scaling mask tensor of shape (W*S) containing the per-shard scale factors, then perform all forward scaling as element-wise multiplication and all inverse scaling as element-wise division in single dispatches per iteration. Maintains 8 all_reduce dispatches but reduces element-wise operations to 8 forward + 8 inverse = 16 vectorized multiplications with better SIMD utilization.

strategies.name: Pipelined double-buffering across iterations
strategies.desc: Overlap computation of iteration i+1's scaling with communication of iteration i's all_reduce by maintaining two buffers and launching operations asynchronously. Still requires 8 all_reduce operations but attempts to hide scaling latency behind network transfers. Total dispatches remain similar but wall-clock time improves through parallelism.

strategies.name: Algebraic transformation to reduce all_reduce count
strategies.desc:
Observe that the pattern (scale → all_reduce → inverse-scale) repeated 8 times might be algebraically reducible. Attempt to factor or combine consecutive operations, potentially merging multiple all_reduce calls by accumulating intermediate scaled results locally before fewer collective operations. If successful, could reduce from 8 to 4 or fewer all_reduce dispatches at the cost of larger intermediate buffers.
